claims.text: Replacing full thermodynamic integration with an LCP scheme using an MTP will reduce computational cost by an order of magnitude while preserving melting-point accuracy.
A liquid-structure-descriptor loss will prevent the MTP from collapsing toward the BCC crystal minimum during perturbation.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the disordered liquid structure of the Ta-based HEA.
Ab initio thermodynamic integration is computationally prohibitive for the target Ta-based HEA.
The MTP will be trained on data enriched with high-temperature liquid snapshots and selected local coordination environments.
Localized nonequilibrium perturbations and reweighting, such as Bennett Acceptance Ratio, can replace the global thermodynamic-integration path by operating only on liquid-like clusters.
The simulations will use 1 atm, temperatures within 50 K of the estimated melting point, and an MTP cutoff radius of 5.5 Å.
Perturbations will be strong enough to break local BCC symmetry but too weak to cause a global phase transformation in one step.
Transient icosahedral or distorted-polyhedral clusters within the BCC lattice act as liquid nucleation seeds.
MTP tensorial descriptors accurately represent these liquid-like clusters, whereas EAM misses them because it relies on radial information alone.
Training the MTP with a loss that penalizes the energy of liquid-like configurations enables efficient sampling of the liquid basin.
Solid–liquid free-energy differences in the target alloy are dominated by local structural fluctuations.
Local perturbation and reweighting can bypass global phase-transition barriers and calculate the solid–liquid chemical-potential difference.
The predicted melting temperature will be within 2% of high-fidelity ab initio benchmarks.
Computational time per data point will be reduced by a factor of 10–20 relative to DFT thermodynamic integration.
The method will predict melting-point suppression caused by configurational entropy in the multicomponent system.
The method is expected to apply to refractory BCC HEAs with moderate-to-high atomic-size mismatch but may fail for directionally bonded systems or liquids with unrepresented chemical ordering.
Insufficient representation of target-alloy liquid environments may cause MTP extrapolation collapse, artificial solid stabilization, or incorrect liquid entropy.
The local-perturbation assumption may fail if long-range elastic interactions dominate the solid–liquid free-energy difference.

The hypothesis is falsified if blind-transfer MTP predictions differ from target-system AIMD by more than 5% in melting temperature, by more than 0.1 Å⁻¹ in the first S(q) peak position, or by more than 10% in peak intensity.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the added loss prevents collapse to the crystal and supports liquid sampling, while the mechanism describes it as penalizing the energy of liquid-like configurations. Taken literally, raising or penalizing liquid-state energies would destabilize the liquid rather than improve access to its basin; the intended meaning may instead be penalizing prediction error on liquid configurations.
